summary: Round 2 answers round 1's major finding correctly and the answer reproduces by measurement. On a throwaway worktree at the staged bytes (501 tests, sweep at its 1,000-seed default, baseline green): moving `refusalsSeen++` below the carve-out reds exactly the two cases the rewritten comment now names -- aRefusalBLAMINGANOTHERPODIsCountedAndTheReleaseIsNotCredited and TWORefusalsBLAMINGANOTHERPODCountTheWINDOWOnce -- with CommitProtocolSweepTest green, so 'caught by A and by B, survives the sweep' is exactly true and complete. Every other measured claim in the cell and the javadocs re-reproduces: continue->break reds only aPARTITIONRefusalAFTERANonPartitionFaultIsSTILLCounted; the deleted break reds only TWORefusalsBLAMINGANOTHERPODCountTheWINDOWOnce; writesBefore=0 reds only aSECONDWindowIsNotCreditedForTheFIRSTSWrite (sweep green, so 'the sweep does not catch it' holds); before=0 and refusalsSeen=0 each red refusalsACCUMULATEAcrossWindowsAndAreNotRECOUNTED AND the sweep, which is what the per-case wording now says instead of round 1's blanket 'SOLE killer'. The compound claim also reproduces: LocalSequencer.close's release swapped for a stat reds the gracefulReleases floor, and the same swap plus writesBefore=0 leaves the sweep green with only the new case red. The new M5.57 row is true in both halves: refusedForAnotherPod++ -> = 1 survives all 501 tests including the sweep, and released++ -> released = 1 survives the new case while the sweep kills it. The pronoun fix is sound (CommitProtocolSweepTest.java:396 does assert gracefulReleasesRefused isZero, and 38 is the refusals-seen figure), list really does draw its unreachable above refuseIfPartitioned (FaultInjectingStore.java:668 before :672) so the sibling case was necessary, and TWORefusalsInOneWindowAreCountedTWICE really asserts 2/0. No src/main file is touched and nothing here changes any object-store request rate. One new false citation came in with the tier fix.

findings.what: The sentence written by round 2 to justify the tier correction cites a javadoc that does not say what it claims: 'the tier (these cases build `MemoryBinStore`, which testing.md puts at T1 and this class's own javadoc has called T1 since M5.29)'. The nearest antecedent of 'this class' is GracefulReleaseMeterTest, whose cases the sentence is labelling -- and the string T1 has NEVER appeared in sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java: `git log -S T1 -- .../GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java` returns no commit at all, and the staged file contains zero occurrences of T0 or T1. Under the only other reading, GracefulReleaseMeter, the javadoc does say 'the T1 case' (GracefulReleaseMeter.java:217) but since M5.28 (0e0db0f), touched again at M5.31 (d48547a) -- never M5.29 (6f1e724), whose contribution is the backlog phrase 'T1 cases now pin it' in its own done cell, which is the backlog record and not a javadoc. So one element of the citation is false on either reading. The testing.md half is right (T1 is 'component with fakes | MemoryBinStore') and the correction itself -- dropping T0 -- is correct; it is the supporting provenance that is invented.
findings.failure_scenario: The cell is the durable record and M5.56 exists precisely because javadoc citations are expected to grep. A later author checking the tier vocabulary of this class greps GracefulReleaseMeterTest for T1, finds nothing, and either re-opens the tier question that round 2 just closed or concludes the cell's other, genuinely measured claims were asserted with the same care. It also credits M5.29 with a label M5.28 wrote, which is the same misattribution family the row itself is closing -- M5.35's own text insists on the distinction between what is in a javadoc and what only a backlog cell says ('it is NOT in either accessor's javadoc, so grepping the javadoc for it finds nothing').
findings.evidence: worktree at staged bytes, sequencer module 501 tests green at baseline. `git show :.../GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java | grep -c 'T1\|T0'` = 0; `git log -S "T1" -- .../GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java` = empty; `git log -S "T1" -- .../GracefulReleaseMeter.java` = d48547a (M5.31), 0e0db0f (M5.28); the single surviving occurrence is GracefulReleaseMeter.java:217 'which is why the T1 case builds the situation'.
